translate_en|mods/SunIsGone/common/media: You would have to go outside for that.
Nothing is burning nearby. Snow needs a fire before it is water.
The ground keeps giving up its heat. Crops take the frost, the animals follow, and staying warm becomes the whole problem.
At sixty below a fire is fighting a much bigger gradient and burns through fuel to stay lit. You never lose the ability to make fire - you lose the ability to leave one burning all night for free.
The temperature falls towards this and never quite arrives. It halves the remaining distance roughly every twenty days.
Below about -25 the dead start dropping where they stand, and they stay where they fall. Give it long enough and the county is bodies in the snow and nothing else.
Dead tissue does not move well at twenty below. They slow as the world cools - and they loosen up again near anything warm.
Cut power and water at hour zero
The grid dies the moment the sun does. It was never an outage - the draw went somewhere else.
How complete the dark is. 100 is a sky with nothing left in it. Lower this if you cannot see enough to play.
Nothing is heating the ground, so nothing is moving the air. The wind dies out and the cold ground fogs over.
Prints the cold, thinning and fuel numbers once a minute. Only useful if something looks wrong and you want to know which system is doing it.
Remove every zombie until the sun goes. Knox is silent and completely still, and nothing tells you why.
Below freezing, open barrels and collectors slowly give up whatever is in them - and stop being a way to bank the snowfall. Snow has to be carried in and melted instead.
Scales the extra fuel deep cold costs you. 0 turns the penalty off without disabling the rest.
Each night's horde as a share of the one before. They are freezing out there, and it shows.
How many should be coming for you on the night the sun goes out. Scaled by your own population setting.
Hour zero takes the taps, and after the last snowfall nothing comes out of the sky. Snow has to be carried in from outside and melted beside a fire.
Every midnight the dead turn and walk at you. The first night is everything the county still has; it only sends more if the county cannot muster enough on its own.
Step outside and the music stops. Out there nothing is scoring this. Get back under a roof, or into a car, and it comes back.
Extra days before the sun goes
It always happens at midnight. 0 means the very next 00:00 - the rest of your first day. Raise this to add whole days on top. You are given no countdown in game - that is the point.

A floor, not a fixed number. The mod counts how many the county actually held during the preparation day - under your population multiplier, your preset, your map - and sends back whatever is larger. On Apocalypse in a town that is a town's worth.
At hour zero every station the game shipped with goes off the band for good - news, talk, emergency broadcast, all of it. Other mods' stations are left alone, and VHS tapes still play.
The sky still holds its water when the sun goes. It comes down as snow, all of it, and then the sky is empty for good.
How buried the world ends up. The snow only ever builds; at these temperatures it never goes.
How long it takes the sky to empty. After this nothing falls again, and nothing melts either.
How far the warmth of a fire or a running generator reaches. Everything inside it moves like the cold never happened.
How far the deep cold slows them. Lower is slower. This is the reward for going out into the worst of it.
The county was empty all day. When the sun goes, it is not empty any more.
